name: Aalto University
summary: Technology, business and design university in Espoo; 11 English bachelor's options, each admitting you to a bachelor's and a master's.

ib.text: IB applicants go in admission round B, ranked on IB grades with national scoring tables. HL and SL score the same; engineering options need advanced maths at 6. No English test needed.

programmes.name: Design and Media
programmes.about: Visual communication, industrial and digital design studied together, crossing art, media and technology, with a Nordic, human-centred and sustainable approach to design.
programmes.overview: You work across visual communication, industrial design and digital design, starting with design fundamentals, strategic identity and sustainable design, and moving into thematic studios. Teaching is hands-on and process-based, mixing workshops, seminars and group projects with feedback sessions, and the third year ends with a bachelor's thesis; exchange and internships are encouraged. Later you choose a track such as Collaborative and Industrial Design, Fashion and Textile Design, Creative Sustainability, New Media, or Visual Cultures and Contemporary Art. Graduates work in communication, interaction, product, service and strategic design, or continue to a master's.
programmes.ib: IB grades do not count: preliminary assignments, intake assignments and an interview decide.
programmes.selectionNote: Preliminary assignments (pass/fail) due 29 Jan 2027, 15:00; intake assignments due 31 Mar; interview 3–7 May. Scored out of 100; grades do not count.

programmes.name: Economics
programmes.about: Economic theory with a strong quantitative toolkit: data analysis, programming and econometrics, applied to real-world questions. Admits you to a 3+2 bachelor's and master's.
programmes.overview: The programme combines economic theory with mathematics, statistics and programming, and the first year includes a course on big societal issues such as inequality, ageing, migration and climate change. You build your own study plan with a minor, for example data science, and can spend a semester abroad at a partner university. Teaching is on campus in Otaniemi, a short ride from central Helsinki, and the degree ends with a bachelor's thesis under a faculty supervisor. It is linked to the Helsinki Graduate School of Economics, and graduates become analysts, consultants, advisers or researchers, with a place in the Aalto master's programme.
programmes.ib: Economics scoring table; advanced maths at 2 or basic maths at 4.

needs.note: Basic maths (AI SL) at grade 4 also counts.

programmes.selectionNote: Round B: ranked on IB grades with the national economics table. 35 of the 50 places are in round B, 28 kept for first-time applicants; a few go on SAT.

programmes.name: Finance
programmes.about: Finance, analytics and strategic decision-making built on business and economics, with attention to socially responsible investment and impact beyond the financial return. New in 2027.
programmes.overview: You study financial markets, investment analysis, risk management and corporate finance, backed by quantitative methods and data analytics, and learn how firms are valued and capital is allocated sustainably. Courses lean on teamwork and cases, with guest lectures and company collaboration, and a closing course looks at the role of finance in society before the bachelor's thesis in year three. A flexible minor can come from technology, design or economics, or you can swap it for an exchange. The student association Aalto Finance runs events and trips to financial centres. Graduates become analysts, consultants and portfolio managers, and continue to the Aalto master's in finance.
programmes.ib: Economics scoring table; advanced maths at 2 or basic maths at 4. SAT/ACT is an optional second route.

needs.note: Basic maths (AI SL) at grade 4 also counts.

programmes.selectionNote: Round B: ranked on IB grades with the national economics table; a few round-B places go on SAT/ACT. New programme, so no past cut-off.

programmes.name: International Business
programmes.about: Marketing, accounting, management and entrepreneurship taught through real business cases and teamwork, with data skills for evidence-based decisions, on the Otaniemi campus.
programmes.overview: You learn marketing, accounting, management, entrepreneurship and business ethics, then pick a theme package such as global supply chains, entrepreneurship, marketing or people management, with data analysis running through the courses. Real business cases, group projects and presentations are the main way of working, and an exchange semester abroad is built into the degree, followed by a capstone course. Electives can come from other Aalto schools, and options include an IT minor or the selective Aalto Founder School. Graduates work as project or business development managers, marketers, consultants and entrepreneurs, and the degree leads into the Aalto master's in business.
programmes.ib: Business scoring table; any maths at grade 2. SAT/ACT is an optional second route.
programmes.selectionNote: Round B: ranked on IB grades with the national business table; 38 round-B places on certificates and 7 on SAT/ACT, 40 more in round A.

programmes.name: Chemical Engineering
programmes.about: Chemistry fundamentals with a strong base in mathematics, programming and machine learning, leading to process engineering, biotechnology and sustainable industry.
programmes.overview: The first years cover mathematics, programming, machine learning, chemistry, physical chemistry and biochemistry, with a focus on sustainable processes in bioproducts and biotechnology. You learn through lectures, group work and laboratory courses, moving from guided exercises to more open projects, with industry guest lecturers and a bachelor's thesis. Electives point towards master's paths in biotechnology, chemical and metallurgical engineering, or chemistry and materials science, and exchange is possible at partner universities. Graduates enter the chemical, semiconductor, biotech, food, pharmaceutical and electronics industries, or go on to research.
programmes.ib: Advanced maths (AA SL/HL or AI HL) at grade 6.
programmes.selectionNote: Round B: ranked on IB grades with the national technology table. 15 of the 35 places are in round B, 11 of them kept for first-time applicants.

programmes.name: Computer Engineering
programmes.about: Mathematics, physics and computer science with hands-on programming and electrical engineering, joining hardware and software for fields such as AI, IoT and telecoms.
programmes.overview: You combine mathematics, physics, programming and electrical engineering with computer science, covering computer architecture, low-level programming, microelectronics, embedded systems and signal processing, plus themes such as AI, the Internet of Things and network security. Lectures and seminars go together with frequent group work and lab projects, including work around a RISC-V microprocessor built by Aalto students. Exchange studies and internships abroad are options. Graduates continue to master's studies in electronics or computer and information sciences, or work as software, hardware, network or embedded engineers.
programmes.ib: Advanced maths (AA SL/HL or AI HL) at grade 6.
programmes.selectionNote: Round B: ranked on IB grades with the national technology table. 18 of the 40 places are in round B, 13 of them kept for first-time applicants.

programmes.name: Data Science
programmes.about: Mathematics, statistics and machine learning combined to extract insight from data and build predictive models, preparing you to work as a digitalisation expert.
programmes.overview: The first year builds foundations in mathematics and programming, the second deepens them with optimisation, statistical inference and machine learning, and the third brings a bachelor's thesis, a seminar and optional advanced courses. Lectures are paired with project work, so you practise building data-driven models that make predictions. The degree draws on Aalto's research links with the Finnish Center for Artificial Intelligence and on collaboration with companies and research institutes. Graduates work as data scientists, engineers or technology entrepreneurs, and the master's route leads to computer science or mathematics and operations research.
programmes.ib: Advanced maths (AA SL/HL or AI HL) at grade 6.
programmes.selectionNote: Round B: ranked on IB grades with the national technology table. 11 of the 30 places are in round B, 8 of them kept for first-time applicants.

programmes.name: Digital Systems and Design
programmes.about: Electrical engineering joined with engineering design: networking, automation, programming and machine learning, plus project work with industry partners.
programmes.overview: You study networking, control and automation, electronic circuits, embedded systems and machine learning, programming in languages such as Python, C++ and Matlab, and you add design thinking and electronic prototyping. Multidisciplinary team projects, industrial projects and a hands-on final project tied to the thesis give you practical experience, and part of the degree can be taken abroad on exchange. The mix of electrical engineering and design is the programme's particular character, and you work alongside students from business, arts and computer science. Graduates go on to the Aalto master's in electrical engineering or to roles in automation, electronics and simulation engineering.
programmes.ib: Advanced maths (AA SL/HL or AI HL) at grade 6.
programmes.selectionNote: Round B: ranked on IB grades with the national technology table. 18 of the 45 places are in round B, 13 of them kept for first-time applicants.

programmes.name: Mechanical and Civil Engineering
programmes.about: Classical mechanical and civil engineering taught through computational simulation and programming, building virtual models of physical systems; leads on to Aalto master's in mechanical, civil or geoengineering.
programmes.overview: You study applied mathematics (calculus, linear algebra, statistics, numerical methods), engineering fundamentals such as fluid mechanics, thermodynamics and mechanics of materials, and computing, including programming, algorithms and finite element methods. The distinctive angle is numerical simulation and programming applied to mechanical and civil problems. You solve real engineering challenges in team projects, use industrial engineering software and finish with a thesis; a semester abroad or summer courses at partner universities are possible. Master's options include mechanical engineering, civil engineering, geoengineering and advanced energy solutions, leading to work as structural, energy or naval engineers.
programmes.ib: Advanced maths (AA SL/HL or AI HL) at grade 6.
programmes.selectionNote: Round B: ranked on IB grades with the national technology table. 18 of the 45 places are in round B, 13 of them kept for first-time applicants.

programmes.name: Quantum Technology
programmes.about: Quantum physics, mathematics, computer science and electrical engineering for computing, communication and sensing, with lab work and master's-level topics early on.
programmes.overview: The major joins quantum physics, mathematics, computer science and electrical engineering, covering quantum materials, circuits and information processing, plus programming, electromagnetic fields, machine learning and quantum laboratory experiments. Lectures, seminars, group and project work run alongside hands-on lab work, including experiments with the AaltoQ20 quantum computer. It is run jointly by the schools of Science and Electrical Engineering, with research ties to VTT and the EU Quantum Flagship. Graduates work as quantum computer engineers, chip designers, software developers and algorithm engineers, or continue to a master's in quantum technology, materials physics, electrical engineering or computer science.
programmes.ib: Advanced maths or physics at grade 6.
programmes.selectionNote: Round B: ranked on IB grades with the national technology table. 15 of the 35 places are in round B, 11 of them kept for first-time applicants.

programmes.name: Technology, Business and Design
programmes.about: A first year spent on technology, business and design together in one class (maths, programming, finance, strategy, design), then a major in one of the three. New in 2027.
programmes.overview: You study mathematics, programming, strategic management, corporate finance, global economics and design process skills, with a focus on responsible, sustainable technology. In the first year you choose a major in technology (mechanical and civil engineering, computer and data science, or digital systems and design), in business, or in design and technology. Teaching combines team projects, industry collaboration and iterative design work, a year-long product development project in the design track, and a bachelor's thesis, with minors and electives to tailor the degree. The programme connects to Aalto's startup community, and graduates go into software, data science, product design, consulting and founding companies.
programmes.ib: Advanced maths at grade 6 plus a passed preliminary assignment, published 17 December 2026.
programmes.selectionNote: Pass the preliminary assignment (published 17 Dec 2026), then you are ranked on IB grades. Places are to be announced by October 2026.

notes: Aalto runs its own application on Studyinfo, not the national joint application, so its window closes on 22 January 2027 rather than the 21st.
You can choose at most three study options in one round, and you are admitted to only one.
Every bachelor's place comes with the right to continue to a named Aalto master's, so you are admitted to a 3+2 year path.
